name: Powder Pink
lede: Powder Pink is a pale, slightly purplish pink that Maerz and Paul dated to 1926, later folded into the ISCC-NBS dictionary of color names in 1955.

sections.title: A pale pink in the dictionaries
sections.body:
Maerz and Paul entered this pink at plate 3 E 7 of their 1930 color dictionary, dating the name to 1926 [1]. The National Bureau of Standards placed it in ISCC-NBS block 29 in 1955, describing it as a moderate yellowish pink, a reading our library finds within 2.5 units of the hex value #FFB2D0 [1].

In Lab coordinates it measures lightness 80.5 and chroma about 32, among the lighter, less saturated pinks in our library [1]. Its nearest neighbor is [[cotton-candy|Cotton Candy]] at #FFBCD9, under five units away, with [[carnation-pink|Carnation Pink]] a little further toward true pink [1]. Set beside [[queen-pink|Queen Pink]], a paler, greyer pink from the same 1955 dictionary, Powder Pink reads brighter and warmer [1]. The word *powder* describes the pale, chalky look of the tone, the same sense used for [[powder-blue|Powder Blue]], not any pigment called powder [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive carries this color across at least 1 percent of its canvas, within CIEDE2000 4 of it, as photographed [2]. That describes this archive's photographs of aged, varnished paintings, not painting as a whole, and a computed color match is never proof of a particular pigment [2].
